_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Calling CRM's processes. Read by:
- app/rto-crm/RtoCrmClient.js  (the Process switcher, and which processes an agent may see)
- api/_lib/tabs.js             (so the admin Permissions UI can grant a process)
- scripts/assign_leads.py      (business hours - whether auto-assignment may run now)
Under api/_lib/ because deploy.yml bundles only api/ into the Lambda; anywhere else and
tabs.js would throw at runtime. Same reasoning as leadAssignmentRules.json.
ACCESS: a process key doubles as its tab_key in report_tab_permissions (card_key
'calling'). An agent sees a process only if they hold that row - i.e. only invited agents
can work a process, enforced server-side by getSession()/getUserTabPermissions rather than
by the browser. Admins (users.is_admin) get an empty tabPerms, which means unrestricted.
Note the localStorage 'rto_agent_roster' is NOT access control - it is a UI convenience
any agent can edit from DevTools, which is why invitations live in the database instead.
BUSINESS HOURS gate AUTO-ASSIGNMENT ONLY. Outside the window assign_leads.py assigns
nothing, but an agent can still open, claim and dispose leads they already hold - a call
that already happened must always be recordable (see openDisp).
Times are local wall-clock in the process's own timezone, `end` exclusive. Days use names
so nothing depends on whether a language counts weekdays from Sunday or Monday.
`implemented: false` means the process has no workspace yet - the CRM shows a panel
explaining what it still needs. Each is expected to bring its own calling fields,
dispositions and data source; none of them share RTO's.

processes.label: RTO Calling
processes.blurb: Return-to-origin leads from the RTO "Data" sheet tab.

processes.label: NDR Calling
processes.blurb: Non-delivery-report leads. Needs its own source sheet/table, the NDR attempt fields (courier reason, attempt count, next-attempt date) and an NDR disposition list - none of which map onto RTO's columns.

processes.label: Detractor Calling
processes.blurb: NPS detractors to call back. Source would be mcaff_dwh.nps_delivery / nps_product (already used by the NPS charts), keyed on response_id with the survey's own score and verbatim feedback rather than an order/AWB.

processes.label: Product KYC Calling
processes.blurb: Product feedback KYC calls. Source is the "Product feedback KYC" workbook (see scripts/productkyc_config.py), where every product tab has its own bespoke question schema - so the calling form is per-product, not one fixed set of fields.
